scope: Independent source-only review of broker runtime proposal Vec-capacity admission v2
verdict: No additional source blocker found in this limited scope; hosted compiler, strict lint and runtime/WAL controls must pass before qualification.
checks: Confirmed the preimage also matches git show at the pinned commit, exact v2 patch forward/reverse reconstruction and byte hashes.
V1 failed rustfmt; independently formatted v1 and v2 normalize to identical v2 bytes, and v2 rustfmt --check passes.
The shared helper uses exactly the original max(frame_bytes, fetch_bytes, controller_request_bytes) expression both in the configured command-envelope calculation and proposal capacity validation.

Source shows the existing nonempty/record-length guard remains and the new capacity guard executes before constructing or admitting the Command. A Vec at or below the existing accounted payload ceiling is moved through the helper and into Command without a clone/shrink/copy at admission.

The new controls propose saturating all public client permits, assert InvalidConfig with zero newly constructed admission/command owner peaks, and compare last position, durable-operation counters and complete bounded metadata WAL bytes; no runtime test was executed.

The positive control intentionally supplies a Vec with capacity above record_bytes but within the existing command ceiling, elects a single-voter leader, and asserts a successful append. The direct helper test checks pointer/capacity preservation.
compatibility: Inputs with valid length but capacity above the command payload ceiling newly return Error::InvalidConfig before admission; invalid input retains its pre-admission precedence even when a runtime is stopped or busy. No new error variant is added. Vec capacity within the ceiling is not narrowed to record_bytes.
limitations: No Rust compiler, Cargo, Clippy, native tests, network, benchmark or publication performed; proposed test behavior remains unobserved.

The WAL control compares metadata.wal bytes and election durable-state counts, not the exact election.wal bytes; admission gauges and a saturated semaphore additionally witness the intended pre-admission boundary if the test runs.
The negative check is performed before leader election; its permit and owner witnesses are essential to distinguishing early rejection from a follower NotLeader result.

Caller-owned unpolled or admission-waiting futures can retain an arbitrary aggregate number of individually allowed vectors, and returned outputs are caller-owned; this change does not bound those allocations, allocator overhead, kernel buffers or RSS.
The separate standalone ControllerHandler request/spare queue capacity gap is not fixed by this patch.
